items.title: Harvard-led Genesis team details $12 million AI quantum error-correction project
items.date_basis: Genesis Intel repository addition date America/New_York; original source published November 20
items.summary: Harvard describes the $12 million Application-Aware Error Correction Codesign for Scientific Quantum Computing (ASQC) project, part of DOE's previously announced October Phase II Genesis awards. Led by Mikhail Lukin with MIT, Cornell, three DOE laboratories and industry partners, the project aims to use AI to design and test quantum error-correction codes adapted to scientific applications. The November 20 feature provides new technical and collaboration details, not a newly awarded grant.
items.affiliation_evidence: Harvard Gazette explicitly identifies ASQC as one of the 12 Phase II Genesis Mission awards announced in October; Cornell independently confirms participation.

items.title: Berkeley Science AI Platform expands planned computing access for Genesis research
items.date_basis: First repository addition; America/New_York calendar date. Preserve through refreshes and imports.
items.summary: Schmidt Sciences support will establish the Berkeley Science AI Platform at NERSC, adding compute and storage using Doudna architecture. Berkeley Lab explicitly links the system to Genesis. User availability is planned for 2028; this is an infrastructure commitment, not an operational launch.
items.what_changed: November 16 announcement establishes a philanthropic computing collaboration and dedicated capacity for Schmidt Sciences awardees and UC Berkeley researchers.
items.significance: Broadens access to scientific machine learning infrastructure.
items.affiliation_evidence: Berkeley Lab director Kathy Yelick explicitly identifies this system as contributing to DOE's Genesis Mission. This confirms mission linkage, not a Genesis RFA award.
items.deduplication_note: Absent from 49-item repository and live feed. NERSC and UC Berkeley versions contain substantially identical reporting and are evidence mirrors, not separate additions.

items.title: Biodata Matters for the Genesis Mission
items.source: Georgetown University — Center for Security and Emerging Technology
items.date_basis: Genesis Intel site addition date (America/New_York); original source published November 19
items.summary: Georgetown CSET examines five biological-data challenges facing DOE's Genesis Mission: quantity, distribution, metadata standardization, quality and validation, and accessibility. The analysis recommends coordinated data curation, interdisciplinary expertise and sustained funding for the American Science and Security Platform. This is independent policy analysis, not a DOE announcement or new project award.
items.affiliation_evidence: The original Georgetown CSET article explicitly analyzes the DOE Genesis Mission and its proposed integrated scientific data platform. Its recommendations are the author's analysis, not official DOE policy.

items.summary: Dakota 7.0 adds a Python API for building and running uncertainty quantification, calibration and optimization studies within larger applications, automation pipelines and agentic SI workflows. The release also updates tutorials. No project-specific Genesis Mission affiliation has been verified.
items.affiliation_evidence: The official Dakota release announcement documents the Python API and agentic AI workflow support without identifying a Genesis Mission affiliation.

items.title: Sandia VASt model predicts advanced-alloy properties with limited training data
items.summary: Sandia's VASt machine-learning model uses electron-distribution fingerprints to predict properties of complex metal alloys from tens of training samples. Researchers are testing its limits and validating predictions experimentally. No project-specific Genesis Mission affiliation has been verified.
items.affiliation_evidence: Sandia's official announcement describes collaboration with Georgia Tech and NASA and partial Laboratory Directed Research and Development support; it does not identify this work as a Genesis Mission project.

items.title: FemtoMind reports threefold lattice-QCD simulation speedup with agentic SI
items.summary: Fermilab reports that SI-generated assembly and code optimization made a collaborator's simulations three times faster in a couple of weeks. The American Science Cloud infrastructure partner is developing verified computational workflows for nuclear physics and future DUNE interpretation.
items.what_changed: November 17 feature reports a threefold simulation speedup achieved over a couple of weeks using an SI agent to write and optimize assembly code. The team is moving from exploration toward practical tools for the lattice-QCD community.
items.significance: Could reduce computational costs and improve neutrino-interaction calculations needed to interpret DUNE. Reference code checks correctness; the report does not establish a threefold gain across every workflow.
items.affiliation_evidence: Fermilab explicitly identifies FemtoMind as Genesis-linked via American Science Cloud. Jefferson Lab's official project page independently calls it an AmSC infrastructure partner; DOE's March 27 Genesis presentation lists US Lattice Quantum Chromodynamics Collaboration (FemtoMind), TJNAF/FNAL, among initial AmSC partners.
items.deduplication_note: Absent from current 43-item archive and accessible review records. New measured progress beyond earlier project descriptions.

items.title: ElMerFold accelerates protein-structure training-data generation on El Capitan
participants: LLNL (Brian Van Essen, Nikoli Dryden, Tal Ben-Nun)
items.what_changed: Reports more than 10,700 predicted protein structures per second on 45,200 MI300A APUs, 71.7-fold speedup over an extrapolated baseline, and estimated generation of approximately 41 million structures in 2.5 hours instead of eight days. Gordon Bell finalist; winner not yet announced.
items.significance: Accelerates synthetic training-data production for open biomolecular models and antibody-antigen prediction. Substantive performance update beyond earlier roughly 2,400 structures/second report.
items.affiliation_evidence: LLNL's new article and official ElMerFold project page describe OpenFold distillation and NNSA mission applications without project-specific Genesis attribution. Checked DOE RFA roster, repository project records, LLNL's ten-project Genesis announcement and targeted ElMerFold/OpenFold searches. LLNL's BIND metalloprotein project and common biology themes do not document affiliation for ElMerFold.
items.deduplication_note: Absent from archive and accessible review records; syndicated copies suppressed. Preserve timestamp from this review-repository addition if subsequently published.
items.summary: LLNL, AMD and Columbia report more than 10,700 protein-structure predictions per second on El Capitan, accelerating training-data generation for OpenFold3. The work could speed development of open biomolecular models. No project-specific Genesis Mission affiliation has been verified.

items.what_changed: Lux opened to scientific users and debuted at rank 14 on the 68th TOP500 list with 220.79 petaflops. Approximately half its annual 3.5 million node-hours are allocated to Genesis, with the remainder available to AMD.
items.significance: Adds operational computing capacity for Genesis scientific workflows, including fusion design, materials/manufacturing and Earth-system prediction.

items.deduplication_note: Enhanced existing collector record; OLCF and ORNL copies are the same report. Restored first-added timestamp from commit history, without resetting to review date.

items.title: TEM Agent connects natural-language microscope control with computing and data tools
items.summary: Berkeley Lab's TEM Agent turns natural-language requests into supervised microscopy workflows, connecting advanced electron microscopes with tomography and ptychography tools, NERSC computing and the Crucible data platform. Researchers report processing tasks in seconds instead of hours, with human correction still essential. No project-specific Genesis Mission funding or affiliation has been verified.
items.date_basis: GIH first Genesis News archive addition; America/New_York
items.what_changed: Newly discovered October report describes tested natural-language microscope control through constrained MCP actions, tomography and ptychography workflows, and links to NERSC and Crucible. It reports processing in seconds instead of hours and documents an initial sample-tilt error requiring human correction.
items.significance: Could make sophisticated microscopy workflows more accessible and reduce analysis bottlenecks; this is supervised research capability, not evidence of error-free autonomy.
items.affiliation_evidence: Official article credits DOE Office of Science support without Genesis attribution. Peter Ercius participates in Ceder's Genesis autonomous-lab team (registry project A-WILD), but shared personnel do not establish that TEM Agent belongs to that award. No project-specific linkage verified.
items.deduplication_note: Absent from archive and review candidates. Foundry republication is treated as the same article; separate from SYNAPS-I X-ray imaging articles.

items.title: Brookhaven SI method separates particle-jet signals from collision backgrounds
items.summary: An unpaired, unsupervised generative model reconstructed jet positions, energies and internal structure more accurately than conventional methods in simulated sPHENIX data. Brookhaven explicitly links the work to a Baruch-led Genesis Phase I project; application to experimental data is next.
items.date_basis: GIH first repository addition; America/New_York
items.project: Characterizing Jet Modification in the Quark-Gluon Plasma Using Unsupervised, Cycle-Consistent Generative Learning
participants: Baruch College / RFCUNY (Genesis project lead Stefan Bathe)
Brookhaven National Laboratory (Yeonju Go, Dmitrii Torbunov and colleagues)
items.what_changed: Unpaired, unsupervised generative learning improves reconstruction of jet positions, energies and internal structure in simulated sPHENIX calorimeter data, especially for larger jets. Experimental data application remains future work.
items.significance: Could improve precision in probing quark-gluon plasma without requiring paired training examples unavailable in real experiments.
items.affiliation_evidence: Brookhaven explicitly connects this work to the named Baruch-led Genesis Phase I award. DOE's official RFA roster independently lists the exact project title and Stefan Bathe at RFCUNY / Baruch. The reported underlying study credits LDRD and DOE Office of Science support; linkage does not imply all study funding came from Genesis.
items.deduplication_note: Absent from 39-item archive and science-discoveries review queue; substantive new research report, distinct from archived SYNAPS-I imaging results.

items.title: LLNL Genesis projects advance faster, more accurate atmospheric prediction
items.summary: LLNL reports substantive progress across two Genesis Mission projects. MAGGIE will generate consistent initial conditions for Earth-system predictions, while LLNL's STITCH team is building machine-learning emulators for warm-rain microphysics and turbulence. Related STRATA emulators reduced an ensemble evaluation from an estimated three months to one weekend, providing a practical path to test MAGGIE outputs and improve cloud physics in E3SM.
items.evidence_note: LLNL explicitly states that MAGGIE and STITCH are funded through the DOE Genesis Mission. STITCH independently matches LLNL's verified project record in the official July 2026 Genesis RFA roster.

items.title: Sandia demonstrates continual-learning improvements in AIGM Lite
items.summary: Sandia's three-year AIGM Lite LDRD project has completed core components of a fast-and-slow continual-learning architecture for sensor-data models. Controlled incremental-learning tests reported accuracy above 90 percent versus above 70 percent for the baseline, with novelty detection, human-reviewed updates and unsupervised clustering now being integrated. The official source does not establish Genesis Mission affiliation.
items.evidence_note: Sandia identifies AIGM Lite as an internally funded Laboratory Directed Research and Development project. No official Genesis Mission or verified Genesis-project connection was found.

items.title: EMSL opens FY 2027 Systems Biology Modeling campaign
items.summary: EMSL invites teams to combine multiomics data, metabolic modeling and SI analysis. Reusable workflows will help explain microbial pathways and support biotechnology and critical-material recovery. Proposals due December 1, 2026; work begins December 15. No confirmed Genesis Mission affiliation.

items.title: EMSL opens FY 2027 Quantum Computing for Metallophores campaign
items.summary: EMSL invites researchers to benchmark hybrid classical-quantum methods for microbial metal-binding molecules. Shared reference datasets and validated workflows could support critical-mineral recovery research. Proposals due December 1, 2026; work begins December 15. No confirmed Genesis Mission affiliation.

items.title: EMSL opens FY 2027 NextGen Molecular Workflows campaign
items.summary: EMSL is connecting CoreMS molecular annotation and SIMPLE simulations through SI agents. The campaign will produce interoperable datasets and validated workflows for biodesign and critical-mineral research. Proposals due December 1, 2026; work begins December 15. No confirmed Genesis Mission affiliation.

items.title: EMSL opens FY 2027 Assured SI for Autonomous Biology campaign
items.summary: EMSL invites research teams to evaluate autonomous biological workflows and develop shared reliability diagnostics and reporting standards. This addresses trust and reproducibility in AI-directed experiments. Proposals due December 1, 2026; work begins December 15. No confirmed Genesis Mission affiliation.

Two OU-led teams received nearly $1.4 million in Phase I funding, including Ahmad Ghassemi's machine-learning and physics-based geothermal work and Grant Biedermann's quantum research.
